sentences.text: Hello everyone. Welcome to the Slow English Podcast. I am Emily. Today we will talk about
Talon. Talon is the capital city of Estonia. It is a beautiful city on the coast of the Baltic Sea.
Talon is famous for its old town, colorful buildings and history. The city is small but full of life.
People enjoy walking on the old streets and looking at old towers. Let's explore Talon together
and learn more about this amazing city. Part 2. Where is Talon? Talon is in northern Europe.
It is on the northern coast of Estonia. It is near the sea and many ships and fairies arrive from
Finland and Sweden. The city is surrounded by forests and parks. The air is fresh and clean.
Talon is an important city for business, tourism and culture in Estonia. Part 3. A short history of
Talon. Talon is very old. It was first mentioned over 800 years ago. In the past it was part of
Denmark, Sweden and Russia. People built walls and towers to protect the city.
The old town of Talon is very well preserved. It has cobblestone streets, churches and houses
from the Middle Ages. Today Talon is modern but still keeps its history alive. Part 4. Talon
The old town is the most famous part of Talon. It has narrow streets, old houses and big walls.
The streets are full of shops, cafes and restaurants. One famous place is Town Hall Square
where people meet and celebrate festivals. Walking in the old town feels like going back in time.
Part 5. Talon Landmarks. Talon has many landmarks. One is Tumpea Castle, a big castle on a hill.
Now it is the government building. Another is Alexander Nefsky Cathedral, a beautiful church
with big golden domes. You can also visit Saint Olafs Church, which was once the tallest building
in the world. These landmarks show the history and culture of Talon. Part 6. Nature Around Talon.
Nature is very close to Talon. There are parks, forests and beaches near the city. People enjoy
walking, cycling and relaxing in nature. One famous park is Kadriyorg Park with beautiful gardens and
a palace. Talon is a city where people can enjoy both history and nature. Part 7. Festivals in Talon.
Talon has many festivals every year. One famous festival is the Talon old town days.
Where people celebrate history with music, dance and food. There is also the Talon Music Week
with concerts from many countries. During Christmas, the Christmas market in the town square is very
popular. Festivals bring people together and make the city lively. Part 8. Food in Talon.
Food in Talon is tasty and simple. People eat fish, potatoes, bread and vegetables.
One famous dish is black bread with smoked fish. Other traditional foods include soup with meat or
vegetables and mulled wine in winter. There are also many international restaurants in Talon,
with Italian, Asian and French food. Food is important in Talon, especially when meeting family
and friends. Part 9. People of Talon. People in Talon are friendly, polite and helpful.
Many people speak English, especially younger people. They enjoy music, art and spending time
outdoors. Family is very important and people often meet in cafes, parks or at home.
The culture of Talon is a mix of old traditions and modern life. Part 10. Weather in Talon.
The weather in Talon is cold in winter and mild in summer. Winter is snowy and dark,
but the city looks magical with lights and decorations. Summer is sunny and warm and people
enjoy walking, cycling and sitting outside. Spring and autumn are beautiful with flowers and colorful
leaves. Talon is special in every season. Part 11. Technology and Modern Life. Talon is very modern
and digital. It is one of the smartest cities in the world. People use technology for banking,
government and education. There are many cafes, shops and co-working spaces with computers and
internet. Even though it is modern, Talon still keeps its history alive in old streets and buildings.
Talon is a city of history, culture and nature. You can walk on old streets, visit castles,
eat tasty food and enjoy the parks and see. It is a city where the past and present live
together. I hope you can visit Talon one day and see its beauty with your own eyes. Goodbye or as
they say in Estonian. Hadega.
